discussion_comments.comment_body:
This make the function have the same footprint as the other hashing algorithm so  that you could actively replace one with the other without any other changes to your code. However if we don't need it async, at least resolving it in a promise gives it that capability. I just wanted to replicate the browser behavior as much as possible so that when someone uses it in an async environment( such as a webserver or a request heavy script with multiple instances per something ) they wouldn't hold up other parts of the script while it runs the SHA and Buffer parts of the code unless the eventloop was empty.

NOTE: secure hashing and most crypto functions are actually quite slow( comparatively ). It's why I'm a fan of using the built in apis to make them operate later. If you're using it for a one time use script then it's perfectly fine, however in a webserver you'll either want a callback, or a promise so that it can run when other things are done because of how awfully slow it can be.
